issue.title: Multi-tracker support for engineering skills
issue.body:
## Destination

A spec that lets every engineering skill read and write the same map across GitHub, Linear, and local markdown from one repo, ready to hand to /to-tickets.

## Notes

Consult domain-modeling for the Tracker / Map / Ticket vocabulary. Keep the spec tracker-agnostic; name Linear specifics only where its API forces it.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index: one line per closed ticket -->

- [What do Linear's sub-issue and blocking APIs actually expose over GraphQL?](https://github.com/northwind/skills/issues/41): sub-issues yes, blocking via issue relations of type `blocks`; no server-side frontier filter, so it is computed client-side.
- [Which tracker is canonical when both GitHub and Linear are configured?](https://github.com/northwind/skills/issues/42): GitHub stays canonical for the map; Linear mirrors tickets one way and never writes back.

## Not yet specified

- How the mirror recovers when someone edits a mirrored ticket directly in Linear
- Whether /wayfinder reads the tracker doc every session or caches the choice in the map's Notes
- What contributors with a GitHub account but no Linear seat can see of a mirrored map

## Out of scope

- [Export a month of Linear issues to see how teams actually use cycles](https://github.com/northwind/skills/issues/51): cycle analytics belong to a reporting effort, not this spec.

nodes.title: What do Linear's sub-issue and blocking APIs actually expose over GraphQL?
nodes.body:
## Question

Before we decide how a map lives in Linear, we need to know whether Linear can express parent/child tickets and blocking natively, and whether the frontier (open, unblocked, unassigned) can be queried server-side or has to be computed.

nodes.title: Which tracker is canonical when both GitHub and Linear are configured?
nodes.body:
## Question

A repo can name two trackers. When the map and its tickets exist in both, which one do skills read as truth, and which one is a mirror?

nodes.title: Should a ticket's type live in a label, a custom field, or the body?
nodes.body:
## Question

GitHub carries `wayfinder:<type>` as a label. Linear has labels and custom fields. Pick one representation that survives the mirror and that a human can still filter on in each UI.

nodes.title: What does the tracker doc look like when it names two trackers?
nodes.body:
## Question

Draft `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` for a repo with GitHub as canonical and Linear as a mirror, so we can react to how much of "Wayfinding operations" has to fork per tracker.

nodes.title: Which tracker is canonical when both GitHub and Linear are configured?
Provision a Linear sandbox workspace with API access for the skills bot
nodes.body:
## Question

We cannot judge the mirror without a workspace to write into. Create a sandbox team, an API key scoped to it, and record where the key lives.

nodes.title: How do GitLab's work-item hierarchies map onto parent/child tickets?
nodes.body:
## Question

GitLab is the next most requested tracker. Do epics and work-item children give us the same map/ticket shape, and does GitLab have native blocking on the free tier?

nodes.title: How should a skill resolve an issue reference that exists in both trackers?
nodes.body:
## Question

When a human writes "the caching ticket" or pastes a Linear URL into a GitHub-canonical map, which issue does the skill load, and what does it say back?

nodes.title: Should a ticket's type live in a label, a custom field, or the body?
What does the tracker doc look like when it names two trackers?
What does /triage print when it finds the same bug filed twice across trackers?
nodes.body:
## Question

Mock the triage output for a duplicate that exists as a GitHub issue and a Linear issue with different titles, so we can see whether "refer by name" still reads cleanly.

nodes.title: How should a skill resolve an issue reference that exists in both trackers?
Do we migrate existing GitHub-only maps, or only chart new ones dual-tracker?
nodes.body:
## Question

There are a dozen live maps in GitHub today. Decide whether the dual-tracker spec applies to them retroactively or only to maps charted after it ships.

nodes.title: Export a month of Linear issues to see how teams actually use cycles
nodes.body:
## Question

Pull thirty days of Linear issues with cycle membership so we can see whether cycles should map onto anything in Wayfinder.
